title: Scientific Opinion on Dietary Reference Values for niacin
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (question EFSA-Q-2011-01218).
result: Niacin (nicotinic acid and nicotinamide) is the precursor of the coenzymes NAD and NADP; many dehydrogenases use NAD or NADP or both, and NAD also takes part in non-redox ADP-ribose transfer reactions. About 60 mg of tryptophan yields 1 mg of niacin. Long-term inadequate intake of tryptophan and niacin can lead to pellagra, with photosensitive dermatitis, tongue and mouth soreness, vomiting, diarrhoea, depression and dementia; untreated pellagra results in death from multiorgan failure.
